trade_offs.detail: graph-only chunks now occupy 2.98 of 5 top-K slots on average, versus 0.00 for the control. Vector hits are displaced by graph evidence; the single-hop guardrail shows this did not cost factual retrieval on this corpus, but a corpus with weaker graph precision could suffer.

mean 11.7 ms versus 11.0 ms for the control. The fusion change is arithmetic over an already-built candidate set, so cost is unchanged; both figures are dominated by query embedding and vary between runs.

None of the six tested mechanisms recovers the 2-hop incident-to-procedure family. Hop-1 neighbours of the vector seeds fill the top-K ahead of the hop-2 answer. Depth-level mechanisms (penalty removal, flat hop credit, seed-strength weighting) leave it at 0.000, and both round-3 hypotheses were measured and rejected: multi-seed convergence cost -0.117 recall@5 with 9 regressions, and query-aware rescoring of graph candidates with the production embedding model cost -0.192 recall@5 with 13 regressions at 2.4x the latency. Rescoring fails for a diagnosable reason: the query names a station, so station and incident chunks outscore the procedure chunk that actually answers it, which is the same lexical gap the corpus was built to create.

The 2-hop answer is unreachable by embedding similarity and, structurally, indistinguishable from the irrelevant hop-1 neighbours of the same seed. Separating them requires knowing which relation to follow (caused_by then maintained_by) for this question, which is query intent, not a scalar any static fusion formula can carry. Two honest routes: a relation-aware retriever that conditions edge traversal on the query, or the bounded RLM loop, where the model issues a follow-up retrieval after seeing the incident chunk. The second is already built (rlm/loop.py) and is the case where a reasoning loop should beat any static fusion. Hand-tuned edge-type priors would also lift this family but would encode this dataset's answer paths, so they are excluded as not a fair test.
